description_good_justification: The README opens with what the lab is and does: an offline, end-to-end test lab that runs the real extension and MCP bridge of Commonpost MCP for Thunderbird (the continuation of thunderbird-mcp) in a real Thunderbird, drives them over MCP and checks what Thunderbird actually wrote. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/README.md
interact_justification: Obtain: README "Quick start" (git clone, docker build). Feedback: CONTRIBUTING "Reporting bugs and requesting features" (GitHub issues). Contribute: CONTRIBUTING (pull requests, ground rules, local checks). https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_justification: Contributions are GitHub pull requests; CONTRIBUTING describes the process, the ground rules, the local checks and what a pull request must contain. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING "Ground rules": synthetic data only, xfail for known, publicly tracked issues, scenarios must pass against the latest release of Commonpost MCP for Thunderbird, keep the isolation, pin what you add, test what you change. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#ground-rules
license_location_justification: LICENSE file at the root of the repository. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/LICENSE
documentation_basics_justification: README: purpose, how it works, quick start, writing a scenario, security model, CI, limitations. docs/scenario-format.md: complete scenario reference. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/README.md
documentation_interface_justification: The external interface is the scenario format (input) and the result block and summary (output), documented in docs/scenario-format.md; run-lab.sh usage and exit statuses are documented in the README and in the script header. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/docs/scenario-format.md
sites_https_justification: The project site, repository and downloads are on GitHub, over HTTPS only.
discussion_justification: GitHub issues and pull requests: searchable, URL-addressable, open to new participants, no proprietary client required. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/issues
english_justification: All documentation, code, issues and pull requests are in English.
maintained_justification: Actively maintained: regular commits, CI on every change, weekly Dependabot, Scorecard and fuzzing runs. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/commits/main
repo_track_justification: Git records who changed what and when. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/commits/main
repo_interim_justification: All commits are public, interim ones included; changes to main go through pull requests (enforced by a repository ruleset). https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/pulls?q=is%3Apr
version_unique_justification: The lab is used from main; each version is identified by its git commit ID (the harness also reports its own version string in every result). https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/commits/main
version_semver_justification: No numbered releases yet; the lab is used from main and identified by commit IDs.
release_notes_justification: No releases: the lab is continuously updated and used directly from main. Each change is described in its pull request and commit message.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No releases, and no vulnerability has been reported or fixed.
report_process_justification: Bug reports and feature requests: GitHub issues, as described in CONTRIBUTING. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#reporting-bugs-and-requesting-features
report_responses_justification: No bug report has been submitted yet (repository created in September 2026); we commit to acknowledge every report within 14 days (CONTRIBUTING). https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/issues
enhancement_responses_justification: No enhancement request yet; they are acknowledged within 14 days like bug reports (CONTRIBUTING). https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/issues
report_archive_justification: GitHub issues are a public, searchable archive. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md explains how to report vulnerabilities (privately, never in a public issue) and what is in scope. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/security/policy
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled (Security tab, "Report a vulnerability"), as SECURITY.md explains. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability report has been received in the last 6 months; SECURITY.md commits to acknowledging reports within 7 days.
build_justification: One command builds the lab image: `docker build -t thunderbird-mcp-lab:local harness` (README "Quick start"; also run in CI). https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/README.md#quick-start
build_floss_tools_justification: The build uses only FLOSS: Docker Engine (Moby), Debian, Python, Bash, GnuPG.
test_justification: Automated test suite, run in CI on every pull request and push: static validation of the scenarios, the isolation self-test (selftest/run.sh), the public end-to-end scenarios against the latest release of Commonpost MCP for Thunderbird, and fuzzing of the scenario validator. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/actions
test_invocation_justification: Standard commands, documented in CONTRIBUTING "Working locally" (`python3 harness/lab.py --validate`, `./run-lab.sh`, `selftest/run.sh`). https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#working-locally
test_most_justification: Code coverage is not measured yet; the end-to-end scenarios and the self-test exercise the main paths of the harness and the launcher.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions on every pull request and push to main, plus weekly scheduled runs. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/actions
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING rule 7 "Test what you change": new functionality comes with a scenario, a self-test check or a validator case in the same pull request. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#ground-rules
tests_are_added_justification: Recent changes came with tests, e.g. the fuzz target added together with the validator fix it found (pull request #4). https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/pull/4
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING rule 7 asks for tests with new functionality and to say in the pull request which tests were added. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#ground-rules
warnings_justification: Linters run in CI on every change: shellcheck (shell) and pyflakes (Python); the workflows are audited by zizmor in CI and linted with actionlint locally (CONTRIBUTING). https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/.github/workflows/lab.yml
warnings_fixed_justification: Any linter warning fails the CI; main is clean. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/actions
warnings_strict_justification: shellcheck at all severities, zizmor with its pedantic persona.
know_secure_design_justification: The primary maintainer designed the lab on these principles, documented in the README: fail-safe defaults and least privilege (container with no network, read-only root, no capabilities, unprivileged user; read-only workflow tokens), complete mediation of untrusted input (strict, fuzzed scenario validator), isolation and separation of privilege (code under test never runs on the host or the CI runner), and a minimal, verified trust base (pinned images and actions, signature-verified Thunderbird download). https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/README.md#security-model-of-the-lab
know_common_errors_justification: The maintainer knows the error classes relevant to this kind of software and applies a mitigation for each: command injection (fixed argument vectors, no shell interpolation of input), path traversal and symbolic-link attacks (strict path patterns, links from the tree are never followed), terminal-escape injection (output sanitiser), supply-chain attacks (pinning, Dependabot cooldown, verified downloads), CI script injection and token exposure (zizmor, least-privilege tokens). https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/SECURITY.md
crypto_published_justification: Only published, reviewed algorithms are used: SHA-512 and OpenPGP signatures (gpgv) to verify the Thunderbird download. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/harness/Dockerfile
crypto_call_justification: Cryptography is delegated to dedicated FLOSS tools (gpgv, sha512sum); the lab implements none itself.
crypto_keylength_justification: The lab generates no cryptographic keys; it verifies Mozilla's release signature with Mozilla's published key.
crypto_working_justification: No broken algorithm or mode is used (SHA-512, OpenPGP signatures).
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No SHA-1 or MD5 is used for any security purpose.
crypto_pfs_justification: The lab implements no key agreement protocol.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The lab stores no user passwords (the disposable test mail account exists only inside the container).
crypto_random_justification: The only security nonce (it tags the result block) is read from /dev/urandom in run-lab.sh. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/run-lab.sh
delivery_mitm_justification: Delivered from GitHub over HTTPS; the Thunderbird download is checked with an OpenPGP signature and SHA-512; base images and actions are pinned by digest and commit SHA. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/harness/Dockerfile
delivery_unsigned_justification: SHA512SUMS is used only after its OpenPGP signature has been verified against the fingerprint of Mozilla's primary release key. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/harness/Dockerfile
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: There is no publicly known vulnerability in the lab (none reported, none open in Dependabot or code scanning).
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerability has ever been reported.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credentials in the repository: the full history was scanned with gitleaks (no leaks found), and GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enabled.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (GitHub Actions and Python), zizmor (workflow security, pedantic), shellcheck and pyflakes run on every pull request and push to main. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/actions
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's security queries and zizmor look for common vulnerabilities (injection, cache poisoning, excessive permissions, unpinned dependencies).
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Findings are triaged promptly; the only CodeQL alert so far (cache poisoning) was analysed and found not exploitable, with the reason documented in the workflow. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/.github/workflows/lab.yml
static_analysis_often_justification: On every pull request and every push to main.
dynamic_analysis_justification: ClusterFuzzLite fuzzes the scenario validator on pull requests and weekly; it found a validator bug that was fixed (pull request #4). https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The lab contains no memory-unsafe code (Python and shell).
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The fuzz target asserts the validator's contract (any exception other than ValueError is a failure) and the isolation self-test asserts two dozen invariants. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/fuzz/fuzz_load_scenario.py
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: The only issue found by dynamic analysis (a validator crash found by fuzzing) was fixed in pull request #4. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/pull/4
dco_justification: No DCO or CLA is required: CONTRIBUTING says that contributions are licensed under the repository's MIT license (inbound = outbound), without a sign-off. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
governance_justification: GOVERNANCE.md: roles, how decisions are made (pull requests, ruleset and required checks, isolation changes), and the rules shared with the main repository. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
code_of_conduct_justification: Contributor Covenant 2.1, at the root of the repository. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
roles_responsibilities_justification: GOVERNANCE.md 'Roles' names the maintainer, contributors and users of the lab, what each can do, and the maintainer's tasks. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
bus_factor_justification: One maintainer today; GOVERNANCE.md explains how a second one joins. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
documentation_roadmap_justification: ROADMAP.md: plans for the next year and what is not planned. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/ROADMAP.md
documentation_architecture_justification: docs/architecture.md: launcher, image, harness, scenarios, self-test, fuzzing, CI and data flow. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/docs/architecture.md
documentation_security_justification: docs/assurance-case.md states the security requirements and the known limits (results are data, not proof; shared kernel); README 'Security model of the lab' and SECURITY.md scope. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md
documentation_quick_start_justification: README 'Quick start': build the image, get a tree, run one scenario then all of them. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/README.md#quick-start
documentation_current_justification: Documentation changes in the same pull request as the behaviour (README scenario table, docs/scenario-format.md). Known gaps (eight scenarios missing from the README table, the labHttpIdle step undocumented, the quick-start tag) were fixed together with these documents.
documentation_achievements_justification: The README front page shows and links the OpenSSF Best Practices and Scorecard badges. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/README.md
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The lab is a command-line tool: plain-text output without colour or cursor control, results as TSV and JSON, a Markdown table in the CI job summary. The project site is GitHub.
internationalization_justification: Messages and results are in English only; the users are developers of the add-on.
sites_password_security_justification: The project sites are GitHub; the project itself stores no passwords.
maintenance_or_update_justification: Only main is supported (SECURITY.md); there are no releases. Upgrading is git pull and rebuilding the image (README 'Quick start'); the harness reports its version in every result, and projects that pin a lab commit move the pin. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerability has been reported or resolved in the last 12 months (no advisories). SECURITY.md commits to crediting reporters.
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md 'How a report is handled': acknowledgement within 72 hours, first assessment within 7 days, triage, private fix in a security advisory fork, merge into main, published advisory with credit, notice to projects that pin the lab. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/SECURITY.md
coding_standards_justification: CONTRIBUTING 'Coding standards': ShellCheck (default severity) for shell, pyflakes and standard library only for Python, zizmor (pedantic) for workflows, the validator for scenarios, SPDX license headers. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#coding-standards
coding_standards_enforced_justification: ShellCheck, pyflakes and scenario validation run in the 'Static checks' job and zizmor in its own job; both are required checks of the main-branch ruleset.
build_standard_variables_justification: No native code is compiled: the lab is Python and Bash.
build_preserve_debug_justification: Nothing is compiled, minified or stripped: the image contains lab.py as written, so tracebacks point at the source lines.
build_non_recursive_justification: One Dockerfile (harness/Dockerfile) builds the image; there is no recursive build.
build_repeatable_justification: The lab's software (Python and Bash) is used as source; nothing is generated from it. The Docker image is a local test environment, not a published result, and is not bit-for-bit reproducible: Debian packages are not pinned.
installation_common_justification: git clone and docker build (README 'Quick start'); uninstalling is deleting the clone and the image (docker image rm). https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/README.md#quick-start
installation_standard_variables_justific: Nothing is installed into system locations: the lab runs from its clone, and the image is managed by Docker.
installation_development_quick_justifica: CONTRIBUTING 'Working locally': build the image, validate scenarios, run them, run the self-test and the linters, with one command each. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#working-locally
external_dependencies_justification: harness/Dockerfile lists the base images (pinned by digest), Thunderbird (version and Mozilla key fingerprint) and the Debian packages; workflows pin actions by SHA; Dependabot parses both. The harness uses only Python's standard library. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/harness/Dockerfile
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot alerts and security updates are enabled; Dependabot proposes updates of the actions and both Dockerfiles' base images weekly; Debian packages are installed fresh at each build (CI rebuilds weekly). The Thunderbird version is updated by hand; it runs offline on synthetic data.
updateable_reused_components_justificati: No third-party code is copied into the repository: every component is fetched at build time from a pinned reference (digest, SHA, version) that Dependabot or a one-line change updates.
interfaces_current_justification: No deprecated Python API is used (the validator runs clean under python -W error -X dev on Python 3.13); Dependabot keeps the actions and base images current.
automated_integration_testing_justificat: Every push and pull request to main runs the static checks, the 21 public scenarios in a real Thunderbird and the isolation self-test; results are reported as check status and a job summary. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/actions
regression_tests_added50_justification: One bug of the lab's own code was fixed in the last six months (a validator crash, pull request #4); the fix came with the ClusterFuzzLite target that found it, which runs on pull requests that touch lab.py and weekly; the validator's negative tests now include both inputs that crashed it (a list as step id and as check step). https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/pull/4
test_statement_coverage80_justification: Measured with coverage.py (by hand, not yet in CI): the 21 scenarios, the isolation self-test and the validator's negative tests (selftest/validator-cases.py) cover 82.5% of the statements of harness/lab.py (987 of 1196). The shell scripts, which every run goes through, are not measured. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/selftest/validator-cases.py
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING rule 7 'Test what you change': new functionality comes with a scenario, a self-test check or a validator case in the same pull request. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#ground-rules
implement_secure_design_justification: docs/assurance-case.md section 3 lists the principles applied (least privilege, fail-safe defaults, complete mediation, separation, input validation) and where each is implemented. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The lab implements no cryptographic protocol; it only checks Mozilla's OpenPGP signature and SHA-512 sums with gpgv and sha512sum, in the algorithms Mozilla publishes.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: The lab holds no keys or long-lived credentials. The only credential is the throw-away POP3 login of the local mail server inside the container, written to its own file at each run; CI uses only GitHub's automatic token.
crypto_used_network_justification: The image build downloads over HTTPS only: Thunderbird with curl --proto =https, and Debian packages from https:// apt sources (harness/Dockerfile checks that no http:// source is left). At run time the container has no network; the harness reaches Thunderbird and the mail sink only over its own loopback interface. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/harness/Dockerfile
crypto_tls12_justification: The Thunderbird download requires TLS 1.2 or later (curl --tlsv1.2 in harness/Dockerfile).
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: curl verifies certificates by default and harness/Dockerfile never disables it; git and gh in CI verify GitHub's certificates.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: Certificates are verified before any request is sent, and the downloads send no private information.
signed_releases_justification: The lab publishes no releases and no images; it is used from main.
version_tags_signed_justification: There are no version tags: the lab is identified by commit.
input_validation_justification: Scenarios are checked against allowlists (known keys, fullmatch patterns, ranges, no '..') before anything runs; the validator is fuzzed, and selftest/validator-cases.py checks that 53 invalid scenarios are refused with the expected message; the input header (nonce, length) and the launcher's arguments are checked too. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md
hardening_justification: Each run uses a container with no network, read-only root, no capabilities, no-new-privileges, an unprivileged user and resource limits; set-uid bits are removed from the image; the harness is non-dumpable; output is sanitised.
assurance_case_justification: docs/assurance-case.md: threat model, trust boundaries, secure design principles, common weaknesses countered with their tests, supply chain and known limits. https://github.com/commonpost/thunderbird-mcp-lab/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md
